paragraphs: We were founded in 1846 and incorporated in Delaware in 1925. We develop, manufacture and market a broad range of consumer household and personal care products and specialty products focused on animal and food production, chemicals and cleaners. Our well-recognized brands include ARM & HAMMER® baking soda, cat litter, laundry detergent, carpet deodorizer and other baking soda-based products; OXICLEAN® stain removers, cleaning solutions, laundry detergents and bleach alternatives; BATISTE® dry shampoo; WATERPIK® water flossers; THERABREATH® oral care products; HERO® acne treatment products; TOUCHLAND® hand sanitizers; TROJAN® condoms, lubricants and vibrators; FIRST RESPONSE® home pregnancy and ovulation test kits; NAIR® depilatories; ORAJEL® oral analgesic; XTRA® laundry detergent; and ZICAM® cold shortening and relief products. Seven of those brands are designated as "power brands" because they compete in large categories, and we believe they have the potential for significant global expansion. Those seven brands are ARM & HAMMER®; OXICLEAN®; BATISTE®; WATERPIK®; THERABREATH®; HERO® and TOUCHLAND® and represent approximately 70% of our net sales and profits. Prior to the sale of our VITAFUSION® and L'IL CRITTERS® ("VMS") business at the end of 2025, we included VMS as an eighth "power brand."

We sell our consumer products under a variety of brands through a broad distribution platform that includes supermarkets, mass merchandisers, wholesale clubs, drugstores, convenience stores, home stores, dollar and other discount stores, pet and other specialty stores and websites and other e-commerce channels, all of which sell our products to consumers. We sell our specialty products to industrial customers, livestock producers and through distributors.
FINANCIAL INFORMATION ABOUT SEGMENTS AND PRINCIPAL PRODUCTS

As discussed in more detail below, we operate in three principal segments: Consumer Domestic, Consumer International, and our Specialty Products Division ("SPD"). Refer to Note 18 to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report and the discussion in "Item 7: Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" for information concerning the results of each of our segments.

All domestic brand "rankings" contained in this Annual Report are based on dollar share rankings from Information Resources, Inc. ("IRI") Total US – Multi Outlet ("MULO") for the period ending December 28, 2025. Foreign brand "rankings" are derived from several sources.
The VMS business which was divested on December 31, 2025 is included in all values and statements, unless otherwise noted.

On July 16, 2025, the Company completed the acquisition of Touchland Holding Corp ("Touchland"), the developer of TOUCHLAND® hand sanitizer products (the "Touchland Acquisition"). The Company paid $656.0 million, net of cash acquired, at closing and entered an agreement to pay an additional amount based on 2025 net sales thresholds which will result in a cash payment of $159.0 million to be paid in the first half of 2026. In addition, the Company granted rights to Touchland's founder to receive shares of our common stock valued at $50.0 million, with 50% of such shares vesting at each of the first-and-second year anniversaries of the closing. The value of common stock received by Touchland's founder will be recognized as compensation expense ratably over the two-year vesting period if the individual continues to be employed by the Company. Payment of a $5.0 million portion of the purchase price was deferred related to certain indemnification obligations provided by Touchland's equity holders, which amount, to the extent not used in satisfaction of such indemnity obligations, is payable three years from the closing. The Touchland Acquisition was financed with cash on hand and is managed in the Consumer Domestic and Consumer International segments. Touchland's annual net sales for the year ended December 31, 2024 were approximately $115.0 million.

On May 1, 2025, we announced that we would exit the Flawless, Spinbrush and Waterpik showerhead businesses, which we exited by the end of 2025. These businesses generated approximately $118.0 million of annual Net Sales in 2025. As a direct result of these actions, we recorded a pre-tax charge of $45.6 million (post-tax of $34.5 million) in 2025, of which $25.0 million was recorded in Cost of Sales and $20.6 million was recorded in SG&A. The charge was recorded in the second quarter within the Consumer Domestic segment and was comprised of non-cash charges related to impairments of intangible and fixed assets, as well as charges related to inventory valuation. A reduction to the second-quarter charge was recorded in the fourth quarter, reflecting final costs to exit the Spinbrush business.

On December 9, 2025, the Company announced a definitive agreement to sell the VitaFusion and L'il Critters brands to Piping Rock Health Products, Inc. The sale was completed on December 31, 2025, and included the VitaFusion and L'il Critters brands, relevant trademarks and licenses, and Church & Dwight's former manufacturing and distribution facilities in Vancouver and Ridgefield, Washington.

The VMS brands represented less than 5% of our 2025 net sales. As a result of this transaction, we incurred a one-time, pre-tax charge of $58.5 million (post-tax of $45.6 million) in the fourth quarter of 2025 which is included in Other income (expense), net in the Consolidated Statements of Income.
The decision to reposition our portfolio with these business exits enables us to devote greater focus to our portfolio's faster growing value and premium product lines.

Our founders first marketed sodium bicarbonate, otherwise known as baking soda, in 1846 for use in home baking. Today, this product has a wide variety of uses in the home, including as a refrigerator and freezer deodorizer, scratch-free cleaner and deodorizer for kitchen surfaces and cooking appliances, bath additive, dentifrice, cat litter deodorizer and swimming pool pH stabilizer. We specialize in baking soda-based products, as well as other products which use the same raw materials or technology and which are sold across multiple consumer and professional use categories. Our Consumer Domestic segment includes each of our seven power brands, as well as other well-known brands and household and personal care products. We divide the Consumer Domestic segment into household and personal care product groups.
In 2025, household products constituted approximately 54% of our Consumer Domestic sales and approximately 41% of our consolidated net sales.

Our primary household products include laundry detergents marketed under the ARM & HAMMER, OXICLEAN and XTRA brands, fabric softener sheets marketed under the ARM & HAMMER brand, cat litter under our ARM & HAMMER brand, and household cleaning products under the CLEAN SHOWER®, ORANGE GLO®, and OXICLEAN brands. Our laundry detergents constitute our largest consumer business, measured by net sales.

The following risks and uncertainties, as well as other factors described elsewhere in this Annual Report or in our other filings with the Commission, could, individually and collectively, have a material adverse impact on our business, reputation, financial results, financial condition and/or the trading price of our Common Stock:
• We face intense competition in our markets.

We face intense competition from consumer products companies, both in the U.S. and in international markets. Most of our products compete with other widely-advertised promoted and merchandised brands within each product category and from retailers, including supermarkets, mass merchandisers, wholesale clubs, drugstores, convenience stores, home stores, dollar and other discount stores, pet and other specialty stores and websites and other e-commerce channels, which are increasingly offering private label and retailer-branded brands and generic non-branded products in certain categories, which typically are sold at lower prices, and consumers are increasingly seeking lower cost "private label" products. In China, in particular we face strong competition from local manufacturers offering both generic and branded products. The use of evolving technology to develop more complex pricing models by retailers has led and may continue to lead to pricing pressures in some categories. In addition, an increase in consumers purchasing more "private label" or other lower price brands has increased competition in certain product categories in particular, including diagnostic kits and oral analgesics, and there has been increased consumer shifts to private label products across multiple categories. Shifting consumer behavior, including continuing shifts to online shopping, has also increased competition in e-commerce in many of our categories, from our larger legacy competitors and newer digitally native brands which have increasingly moved into consumer products and staples.

Many of our competitors are large companies, including, among others, P&G, The Clorox Company, Colgate-Palmolive Company, S.C. Johnson & Son, Inc., Nestlé S.A., Haleon plc, Henkel, Reckitt Benckiser Group plc, LifeStyles Healthcare, Kenvue Inc., Pfizer Inc., Bayer AG, NBTY, Inc., Koninklijke Philips N.V., Unilever PLC, Sanofi, Edgewell Personal Care, Panoxyl, Starface, GOJO Industries, Inc., and Peach & Lily. Many of these companies have greater financial resources than we do, and these competitors, as well as new market entrants, may therefore, have the capacity to outspend us on advertising and promotional activities and introduce competing products or adopt new technologies, such as artificial intelligence and machine learning, more quickly, successfully and effectively, and respond more effectively to changing business and economic conditions than we can.

Our products generally compete based on performance, brand recognition, price, value or other benefits to consumers. Significant price competition may require us to reduce the prices for some of our products to price levels that do not offset manufacturing cost increases, to respond to competitive and customer pressures and to maintain market share. Increases to our prices, because of inflationary pressures or otherwise, could cause declining sales of products whose prices we have increased. In response to inflationary pressures and other factors, we have raised prices on many of our products across our global portfolio of brands in recent years. Ongoing periods of high inflation or increased costs resulting from higher tariffs imposed by the U.S. or other countries could lead to additional price increases on these or our other products, adversely impacting demand for our products. Advertising, promotion, merchandising and packaging also have a significant impact on retail customer decisions regarding the brands and product lines they sell and on consumer purchasing decisions. A newly introduced consumer product (whether improved or newly developed) usually encounters intense competition requiring substantial expenditures for advertising, sales promotion and trade merchandising. If a product gains consumer acceptance, it normally requires continued advertising, promotional support and product improvements to maintain its relative market position. If our advertising, marketing and promotional programs, including the use of digital and social media to reach consumers, are not effective, our sales growth may decline.
• A continued change in the retail environment and changing consumer preferences could cause our sales to decline.

The segments are based on differences in the nature of products sold and management organizational structures. In 2025, the Consumer Domestic, Consumer International and SPD segments represented approximately 77%, 18% and 5%, respectively, of our consolidated net sales.

We have experienced increased commodity cost volatility and economic uncertainty primarily due to changes in U.S. trade policies including ongoing reviews and modifications to tariffs and other U.S. trade measures. We continue to evaluate these evolving developments and have taken actions to mitigate their impact on our business, including taking strategic actions for certain business lines (see Strategic Business Decisions below), shifting production and relocating manufacturing operations, finding alternative sources of supply, most notably ceasing the import of substantially all Waterpik flossers and other products from China into the U.S., potentially increasing prices, adjusting inventories, lobbying and seeking exemptions with respect to tariffs. While the tariffs remain fluid, we are focused on managing these challenges. We believe our existing tariff cost exposure will be mitigated through the above-mentioned actions, future additional supply chain efforts and surgical pricing.

This agreement includes the VitaFusion and L'il Critters brands, relevant trademarks and licenses, and the Company's former manufacturing and distribution facilities in Vancouver and Ridgefield, Washington. The transaction closed on December 31, 2025.
CHURCH & DWIGHT CO., INC AND SUBSIDIARIES

The VMS brands represented less than 5% of our 2025 net sales. As a result of this transaction, we incurred a one-time, pre-tax charge of $58.5 (post-tax of $45.6) in the fourth quarter of 2025 which is included in in Other income (expense), net in the Consolidated Statements of Income.
The decision to reposition our portfolio with these business exits enables us to devote greater focus to our portfolio's faster growing value and premium product lines.

In May 2025, the Company entered into an accelerated share repurchase ("ASR") contract with a commercial bank to purchase Common Stock. The Company paid $300.0 to the bank, inclusive of fees, and received 2.8 million shares in May 2025 and 0.3 million shares in August 2025 at an average total share price of $95.71. The Company purchased all 3.1 million shares under the evergreen share repurchase program and used cash on hand to fund the purchase price.

In August and September 2025, the Company executed open market purchases of 3.2 million shares for $300.0, inclusive of fees, of which $170.0 was purchased under the evergreen share repurchase program and $130.0 was purchased under the 2021 Share Repurchase Program (as defined below). The shares were purchased at an average share price of $92.81 and the Company used cash on hand to fund the open market purchases.

In November and December 2025, the Company executed open market purchases of 3.6 million shares for $300.0, inclusive of fees, of which all 3.6 million shares were purchased under the 2021 Share Repurchase Program. The shares were purchased at an average share price of $83.59 and the Company used cash on hand to fund the open market purchases.

On July 4, 2025, President Trump signed into law the legislation formally titled "An Act to Provide for Reconciliation Pursuant to Title II of H. Con. Res. 14" and commonly referred to as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act ("OBBBA"). The legislation includes several provisions that may impact the timing and magnitude of certain tax deductions. Key provisions include the permanent extension of several key elements of the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, including 100% bonus depreciation and an immediate tax deduction for domestic research costs. The tax provisions in OBBBA did not have a material impact on our financial position and results of operations, and had a minimal benefit to operating cash flows.

paragraphs: 本公司於1846年成立，並於1925年在特拉華州註冊為公司。本公司開發、製造及行銷廣泛的消費者家庭及個人護理產品，以及專注於動物與食品生產、化學品及清潔劑的專業產品。本公司知名的品牌包括ARM & HAMMER®小蘇打、貓砂、洗衣清潔劑、地毯除臭劑及其他小蘇打基準產品；OXICLEAN®污漬去除劑、清潔溶液、洗衣清潔劑及漂白替代品；BATISTE®乾洗髮粉；WATERPIK®水牙線；THERABREATH®口腔護理產品；HERO®青春痘治療產品；TOUCHLAND®洗手消毒液；TROJAN®避孕套、潤滑劑及振動器；FIRST RESPONSE®居家懷孕及排卵測試套件；NAIR®脫毛產品；ORAJEL®口腔止痛藥；XTRA®洗衣清潔劑；以及ZICAM®感冒退燒產品。其中七個品牌被指定為"power brands"，因為它們在大型產品類別中競爭，本公司認為它們有潛力進行顯著的全球擴張。這七個品牌為ARM & HAMMER®；OXICLEAN®；BATISTE®；WATERPIK®；THERABREATH®；HERO®及TOUCHLAND®，並代表約70%的淨銷售額與利潤。在2025年底出售VITAFUSION®及L'IL CRITTERS®（"VMS"）業務之前，本公司將VMS視為第八個"power brand"。
本公司透過多種品牌銷售消費者產品，透過廣泛的銷售平台，包括超級市場、折扣商店、連鎖百貨、藥妝店、便利商店、居家商店、美元及其他折扣商店、寵物及其他專業商店，以及網站及其他電商通路，所有這些通路都向消費者銷售本公司產品。本公司將專業產品銷售給工業客戶、畜牧生產者，並透過經銷商進行銷售。
關於分部及主要產品的財務資訊
如後文更詳細說明，本公司經營三個主要分部：消費者國內、消費者國際，以及我們的專業產品部門（"SPD"）。請參閱本年度報告所附合併財務報表的附註18，以及"項目7：管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析與討論"中關於各分部結果的資訊。
本年度報告中所有國內品牌"排名"均根據Information Resources, Inc.（"IRI"）於2025年12月28日結訖的總美國多通路（"MULO"）美元市佔率排名。外國品牌"排名"則來自多個來源。
於2025年12月31日出售的VMS業務，已包含在所有數值與陳述中，除非另有說明。

本公司於2025年7月16日完成對Touchland Holding Corp（"Touchland"）的收購（"Touchland收購"），Touchland為TOUCHLAND®洗手消毒液產品的開發商。本公司於交易關閉時支付了6.56億美元（扣除所獲現金），並同意根據2025年淨銷售額門檻支付額外金額，這將導致於2026年上半年支付1.59億美元現金。此外，本公司授予Touchland創辦人權利，以獲得本公司普通股股份，價值5千萬美元，其中50%的股份於交易關閉後第一及第二年紀念日分別解鎖。若該個人繼續為本公司員工，Touchland創辦人所獲得的普通股價值將於兩年解鎖期間按比例計入薪資費用。與Touchland股東提供的某些賠償義務相關的5千萬美元購股款部分被延後支付，該金額若未用於償還賠償義務，則於交易關閉後三年內支付。Touchland收購由現金資產資助，並由消費者國內及消費者國際分部管理。Touchland於2024年12月31日結訖的年度淨銷售額約為1.15億美元。

本公司於2025年5月1日宣佈將退出Flawless、Spinbrush及Waterpik的淋浴頭業務，並於2025年底完成退出。這些業務在2025年產生約1.18億美元的年度淨銷售額。由於這些行動，本公司於2025年記錄了一筆4,560萬美元的稅前費用（稅後為3,450萬美元），其中2,500萬美元計入銷售成本，2,060萬美元計入營運及一般費用。該費用於2025年第二季在消費者國內分部記錄，包含非現金費用，與無形資產及固定資產的減損有關，以及與存貨評估相關的費用。於2025年第四季，本公司記錄了一筆減額，反映退出Spinbrush業務的最終成本。

於 2025 年 12 月 9 日，本公司宣佈與 Piping Rock Health Products, Inc. 簽訂買賣協議，將 VitaFusion 及 L'il Critters 品牌出售。此交易於 2025 年 12 月 31 日完成，包含 VitaFusion 及 L'il Critters 品牌、相關商標與授權，以及 Church & Dwight 過去在 Vancouver 及 Ridgefield, Washington 的製造與配送設施。
VMS 品牌在 2025 年的淨銷售額中佔比低於 5%。由於此交易，我們在 2025 年第四季產生一次性、未稅費用 58.5 萬美元（稅後 45.6 萬美元），此費用已列入綜合損益表中的其他收入（費用），淨額。
決定透過這些業務退出來重新定位我們的產品組合，使我們能更專注於產品組閤中成長較快的價值型與高階產品線。

我們的創辦人於 1846 年首次將碳酸氫鈉（俗稱小蘇打）推向市場，用於家庭烘焙。今日，此產品在家中的用途已廣泛，包括作為冰箱與冷凍庫除臭劑、廚房表面與烹飪設備的刮痕無痕清潔劑與除臭劑、浴缸添加劑、牙膏、貓砂除臭劑以及游泳池 pH 值穩定劑。我們專門從事以小蘇打為基礎的產品，以及使用相同原料或技術的其他產品，並銷售至多種消費者與專業用途類別。我們的消費者家庭業務部門包含我們的七個主要品牌，以及其他知名品牌與家庭與個人護理產品。我們將消費者家庭業務部門分為家庭與個人護理產品羣組。
2025 年，家庭用品約佔我們消費者家庭業務銷售額的 54%，約佔我們綜合淨銷售額的 41%。
我們的主要家庭用品包括以 ARM & HAMMER、OXICLEAN 和 XTRA 品牌行銷的洗衣清潔劑，以 ARM & HAM默品牌行銷的洗衣柔軟劑片，以 ARM & HAMMER 品牌行銷的貓砂，以及以 CLEAN SHOWER®、ORANGE GLO® 和 OXICLEAN 品牌行銷的家庭清潔產品。我們的洗衣清潔劑是我們最大的消費者業務，以淨銷售額衡量。

paragraphs: 管理階層對於財務狀況與營運成果之討論分析應與我們之合併財務報表一併閱讀。

我們開發、製造與行銷廣泛的消費者家庭、個人護理與專業產品。我們廣為認知的品牌包括 ARM & HAMMER® 烘焙蘇打、貓砂、洗衣清潔劑、地毯除臭劑及其他烘焙蘇打基底產品；OXICLEAN® 污漬去除劑、清潔溶液、洗衣清潔劑與漂白替代品；TOUCHLAND® 手部清潔劑；BATISTE® 乾洗髮；WATERPIK® 水牙線；THERABREATH® 口腔護理產品；HERO® 痘痘治療產品；TROJAN 避孕套、潤滑劑與振動器；FIRST RESPONSE 家用懷孕與排卵測試套件；NAIR 脫毛產品；ORAJEL 口腔止痛藥；XTRA 洗衣清潔劑；以及 ZICAM 感冒緩解產品。其中七個品牌被指定為 "power brands"，因為它們競爭於大型產品類別，我們認為它們有潛在的全球擴張機會。這七個品牌為 ARM & HAMMER®；OXICLEAN®；TOUCHLAND®；BATISTE®；WATERPIK®；THERABREATH®；以及 HERO®，代表約 70% 的我們淨銷售額與利潤。在 2025 年底出售我們的 VITAFUSION® 和 L'IL CRITTERS®（"VMS"）業務之前，我們將 VMS 視為第八個 "power brand"。
我們透過多樣的品牌銷售消費者產品，透過廣泛的銷售平台，包括超市、折扣商店、百貨公司、藥妝店、便利商店、居家商店、美元商店、寵物及其他專業商店，以及網站和其他電商通路，所有這些通路都將產品銷售給消費者。我們將專業產品銷售給工業與商業客戶、畜牧生產者，以及透過經銷商。
我們的業務分為三個應報告分部：消費者國內市場、消費者國際市場與專業產品部門（"SPD"）。這些分部是根據產品銷售的性質與管理組織結構的差異而設立。在 2025 年，消費者國內市場、消費者國際市場與 SPD 分部分別代表約 77%、18% 和 5% 的我們合併淨銷售額。

我們經歷了原材料成本波動增加與經濟不確定性，主要由於美國貿易政策的變化，包括持續的審查與修改關稅及其他美國貿易措施。我們持續評估這些發展，並已採取行動以緩解對我們業務的影響，包括對某些業務線採取戰略行動（見下文戰略業務決策），轉移生產與重新安置製造業務，尋找替代供應來源，特別是停止將幾乎所有 Waterpik 牙線及其他產品從中國進口至美國，可能提高價格，調整存貨，遊說並尋求關稅豁免。雖然關稅仍處於流動狀態，我們專注於管理這些挑戰。我們相信透過上述行動、未來的供應鏈努力與精準定價，我們現有的關稅成本風險將得以緩解。

2025 年 5 月 1 日，我們宣佈將退出 Flawless、Spinbrush 和 Waterpik 浴頭業務。我們在 2025 年底退出了這些業務。這些業務在 2025 年產生了約 $118.0 的年度淨銷售額。我們在 2025 年記錄了一筆 $45.6（稅後 $34.5）的預稅費用，直接由於這些行動，其中 $25.0 記錄在銷售成本，$20.6 記錄在營運及一般及行政費用。這筆費用主要記錄在第二季的消費者國內市場分部，並包含非現金費用，與無形資產及固定資產減損有關，以及與存貨價值有關的費用。在第四季，我們記錄了一筆減少第二季費用的金額，與最終退出 Spinbrush 業務的費用有關。

2025 年 12 月 9 日，本公司宣佈與 Piping Rock Health Products, Inc. 籤訂了出售 VitaFusion 和 L'il Critters 品牌的最終協議。此協議包括 VitaFusion 和 L'il Critters 品牌、相關商標與授權，以及本公司在溫哥華和華盛頓 Ridgefield 的前製造與分銷設施。交易於 2025 年 12 月 31 日完成。
CHURCH & DWIGHT CO., INC AND SUBSIDIARIES
VMS 品牌在 2025 年的淨銷售額中佔比低於 5%。因應此交易，本公司於 2025 年第四季產生一次性、未稅費用 58.5 美元（稅後 45.6 美元），此費用已列入綜合損益表之其他收入（費用），淨額項目中。
決定透過這些業務退出來重新定位產品組合，使本公司能更專注於產品組閤中成長較快的價值型與高階產品線。
2025 年 5 月，本公司與商業銀行簽訂加速股票回購（"ASR"）契約，購買普通股。本公司支付 300.0 美元予銀行（含手續費），並於 2025 年 5 月取得 280 萬股，2025 年 8 月取得 30 萬股，平均總股價為 95.71 美元。本公司於永續股票回購計畫下購入所有 310 萬股，並以現金支應購股金額。
2025 年 8 月及 9 月，本公司於公開市場購入 320 萬股，總金額為 300.0 美元（含手續費），其中 170.0 美元為永續股票回購計畫購入，130.0 美元為 2021 年股票回購計畫購入（如後文所定義）。購入平均股價為 92.81 美元，本公司以現金支應公開市場購股金額。
2025 年 11 月及 12 月，本公司於公開市場購入 360 萬股，總金額為 300.0 美元（含手續費），其中所有 360 萬股均為 2021 年股票回購計畫購入。購入平均股價為 83.59 美元，本公司以現金支應公開市場購股金額。

2025 年 7 月 4 日，總統特朗普簽署成為法律的法案正式名稱為 "An Act to Provide for Reconciliation Pursuant to Title II of H. Con. Res. 14"，常被稱為 "One Big Beautiful Bill Act"（"OBBBA"）。該法案包含若干可能影響特定稅務減免時點與金額的條款。關鍵條款包括永久延長 2017 年稅改與就業法案（Tax Cuts and Jobs Act）若干重要項目，包括 100% 一次性折舊與國內研究成本立即稅務減免。OBBBA 的稅務條款對本公司財務狀況與營運成果未造成重大影響，且對營運現金流僅有微小好處。
下列風險與不確定性，以及本年度報告或其他向委員會提交的文件中所描述的其他因素，可能個別或 collectively 對本公司業務、聲譽、財務結果、財務狀況及/或普通股交易價格產生重大不利影響：
• 我們在市場上面臨激烈的競爭。

我們在美國及國際市場均面臨來自消費產品公司的激烈競爭。我們的大多數產品與每個產品類別中其他廣為宣傳、推廣及販售的品牌以及零售商（包括超級市場、百貨商店、 Wholesale 俱樂部、藥妝店、便利商店、家居商店、美元及其他折扣商店、寵物及其他專門商店以及網站及其他電商通路）競爭，這些零售商在某些類別中 increasingly 提供自有品牌及零售商品牌產品以及一般非品牌產品，這些產品通常售價較低，消費者 increasingly 尋求較低成本的 "自有品牌" 產品。特別是在中國，我們面臨來自本地製造商的強烈競爭，這些製造商提供一般性及品牌性產品。零售商使用演進中的技術來開發更複雜的定價模型，已導致並可能繼續導致某些類別的定價壓力。此外，消費者購買更多 "自有品牌" 或其他較低價位品牌的增加，已增加了某些產品類別的競爭，特別是診斷試劑盒及口服止痛藥，同時消費者在多個類別中也增加了對自有品牌的轉移。消費者行為的改變，包括持續轉向線上購物，也增加了我們許多類別在電商中的競爭，來自我們較大的傳統競爭對手以及較新的數位原生品牌，這些品牌 increasingly 進入消費產品及必需品領域。

我們的許多競爭對手為大型公司，包括但不限於 P&G、The Clorox Company、Colgate-Palmolive Company、S.C. Johnson & Son, Inc.、Nestlé S.A.、Haleon plc、Henkel、Reckitt Benckiser Group plc、LifeStyles Healthcare、Kenvue Inc.、Pfizer Inc.、Bayer AG、NBTY, Inc.、Koninklijke Philips N.V.、Unilever PLC、Sanofi、Edgewell Personal Care、Panoxyl、Starface、GOJO Industries, Inc. 以及 Peach & Lily。這些公司中許多擁有比我們更龐大的財務資源，因此這些競爭對手以及新進市場參與者可能擁有足夠的資源在廣告及促銷活動上超過我們，推出競爭產品或採用新技術（如人工智慧及機器學習）更迅速、成功且有效，並對變動的業務及經濟條件做出更有效的回應。

我們的產品通常根據性能、品牌認知度、價格、價值或其他對消費者有益的特點進行競爭。顯著的價格競爭可能迫使我們降低某些產品的價格至無法抵消製造成本增加的水平，以回應競爭及客戶壓力並維持市場佔有率。因通貨膨脹壓力或其他原因而提高價格，可能會導致我們提高價格的產品銷售量下降。為回應通貨膨脹壓力及其他因素，我們在近年內已提高許多產品的價格，這些產品涵蓋我們全球品牌組合。持續的高通貨膨脹或因美國或其他國家提高關稅而導致的成本增加，可能會導致這些或我們其他產品的進一步價格上漲，對我們產品的需求產生不利影響。廣告、促銷、販售及包裝對零售客戶決定銷售的品牌及產品線以及消費者購買新產品的決定有重大影響。新推出的消費產品（無論是改進或新開發的）通常會遇到激烈的競爭，需要大量支出於廣告、銷售促銷及貿易販售。如果產品獲得消費者接受，通常需要持續的廣告、促銷支援及產品改進以維持其相對市場地位。如果我們的廣告、行銷及促銷方案（包括使用數位及社交媒體來接觸消費者）未能有效，我們的銷售成長可能會下降。
• 零售環境持續變化及消費者偏好改變可能導致我們的銷售下降。
